turns.en: Shall we get you up for a little walk? Take your time, no rush. Hold onto my arm.
turns.cy: Wnawn ni'ch codi chi am dro bach? Cymrwch eich amser — dim brys. Gafaelwch yn fy mraich i.
chunks: Shall we get you up for a little walk?
Wnawn ni'ch codi chi am dro bach?
gafael governs yn, which English's 'onto' does not signal

turns.en: Yes, good idea. I'm stiff as a board lying here.
turns.cy: Ia, syniad da. Dw i'n stiff fel procer yn gorwedd yn fan'ma.
chunks: I'm stiff as a board lying here
Dw i'n stiff fel procer yn gorwedd yn fan'ma
the simile relocates: Welsh is stiff as a POKER, not as a board

turns.en: Good. Nice and slow now - sit on the edge of the bed first, and we'll let your head catch up with you.
turns.cy: Da iawn. Yn ara deg rŵan — steddwch ar ochr y gwely gynta, ac mi adawn ni i'ch pen chi ddal i fyny efo chi.
chunks: HG47; the pace family keeps four knowns on four forms (R4)
sit on the edge of the bed first
steddwch ar ochr y gwely gynta
and we'll let your head catch up with you
ac mi adawn ni i'ch pen chi ddal i fyny efo chi

turns.en: Right you are. Edge of the bed first.
turns.cy: O'r gorau. Ochr y gwely gynta.

turns.en: Take all the time you need. There's no prize for rushing. Ready? Off we go.
turns.cy: Cymrwch yr holl amser dach chi ei angen. Does 'na ddim gwobr am ruthro. Barod? Ffwrdd â ni.
chunks: Take all the time you need
Cymrwch yr holl amser dach chi ei angen
HG48 verbatim; angen takes a possessive object ei, not a direct one
English's copula erases in the elliptical question
the â-propulsion frame (§4) — a verbless Welsh sentence where English needs a verb

turns.en: Further than yesterday? Well, there's a thing.
turns.cy: Yn bellach na ddoe? Wel, dyna i chi beth.
chunks: English's existential of surprise relocates to the dyna i chi presentative

turns.en: Shall we get you up for a little walk? Hold onto my arm.
turns.cy: Wnawn ni'ch codi chi am dro bach? Gafaelwch yn fy mraich i.
chunks: Shall we get you up for a little walk?
Wnawn ni'ch codi chi am dro bach?

turns.en: I feel a bit dizzy when I stand up. Is that normal?
turns.cy: Dw i'n teimlo braidd yn benysgafn pan dw i'n sefyll i fyny. Ydy hynny'n normal?
chunks: I feel a bit dizzy when I stand up
Dw i'n teimlo braidd yn benysgafn pan dw i'n sefyll i fyny
⚠ line — plainest possible; braidd yn for the hedge

turns.en: That's worth knowing. Sit back down a minute. Dizziness when you stand can be the tablets, or just lying down too long - I'll check your blood pressure sitting and standing.
turns.cy: Mae hynna werth ei wybod. Steddwch yn ôl i lawr am funud. Mi fedar penysgafnder wrth sefyll fod yn sgil y tabledi, neu jyst gorwedd yn rhy hir — mi wna i tsiecio'ch pwysau gwaed chi'n eistedd ac yn sefyll.
chunks: ⚠ line — the pre-posed possessive object ei before the verbal noun
Steddwch yn ôl i lawr am funud
Dizziness when you stand can be the tablets
Mi fedar penysgafnder wrth sefyll fod yn sgil y tabledi
⚠ line — English's bare 'be the tablets' relocates to yn sgil, 'in the wake of', which is what the sentence means
or just lying down too long
neu jyst gorwedd yn rhy hir
I'll check your blood pressure sitting and standing
mi wna i tsiecio'ch pwysau gwaed chi'n eistedd ac yn sefyll

turns.en: It's passing now. It does that every time, mind.
turns.cy: Mae o'n pasio rŵan. Mae o'n gneud hynny bob tro, cofiwch.
chunks: Mae o'n gneud hynny bob tro
⚠ line — the full verb, because Welsh has no pro-verb 'do'

turns.en: Then we'll take it extra slow, and I won't let go of you. To the door and back today, nothing heroic.
turns.cy: Mi gymrwn ni hi'n ara deg iawn 'ta, a wna i ddim eich gollwng chi. At y drws ac yn ôl heddiw, dim gorwneud hi.
chunks: Then we'll take it extra slow
Mi gymrwn ni hi'n ara deg iawn 'ta
HG49; the pace family's third form (R4); 'ta the in-that-case tag (S1)
and I won't let go of you
a wna i ddim eich gollwng chi
To the door and back today
At y drws ac yn ôl heddiw
English's adjective relocates to a verbal-noun phrase — 'no overdoing it'

turns.en: To the door and back. I can manage that, I think.
turns.cy: At y drws ac yn ôl. Mi fedra i ddod i ben efo hynny, dw i'n meddwl.
chunks: At y drws ac yn ôl
Mi fedra i ddod i ben efo hynny
the walk's one manage-lexeme, dod i ben

turns.en: Shall we get you up for a little walk? Take your time.
turns.cy: Wnawn ni'ch codi chi am dro bach? Cymrwch eich amser.
chunks: Shall we get you up for a little walk?
Wnawn ni'ch codi chi am dro bach?

turns.en: I'm frightened of falling, see. You will hold onto me, won't you?
turns.cy: Mae gen i ofn syrthio, ylwch. Mi wnewch chi ddal gafael yna i, gnewch?
chunks: fear is possessed in Welsh — mae gen i ofn — where English predicates it as an adjective
You will hold onto me, won't you?
Mi wnewch chi ddal gafael yna i, gnewch?
the verb-echo tag, and its polarity flips: Welsh tags positive where English tags negative
south: mae ofn arna i — AND A REORDER
turns.southLine: Mae ofn cwympo arna i, edrychwch. Fe wnewch chi ddal gafael yno i, gwnewch?

turns.en: I've got you, I promise - I won't let go. And we'll just go to the door and back. Nothing heroic.
turns.cy: Dw i'n eich dal chi, dw i'n gaddo — wna i ddim gollwng. Ac mi awn ni jyst at y drws ac yn ôl. Dim gorwneud hi.
chunks: Dw i'n eich dal chi, dw i'n gaddo
HG49 verbatim — English's have-got becomes a Welsh present progressive of holding
distinct from 'I won't let go OF YOU' → …eich gollwng chi
And we'll just go to the door and back
Ac mi awn ni jyst at y drws ac yn ôl

turns.en: To the door and back, then, if you're holding on.
turns.cy: At y drws ac yn ôl, 'ta, os dach chi'n dal gafael.
chunks: At y drws ac yn ôl
English's particle 'on' erases into the fixed dal gafael

turns.en: Every step. Well done, you - that's further than yesterday. We'll do it again after tea.
turns.cy: Bob cam. Da iawn chi — mae hynna'n bellach na ddoe. Mi wnawn ni o eto ar ôl te.
chunks: HG50 verbatim; the emphatic chi carries English's appositive 'you'
We'll do it again after tea
Mi wnawn ni o eto ar ôl te
the amdani ratifier again; it converges with the 'X it is' family, which is reception and welcome
